questions.question: For the vector equation $\boldsymbol{x}'(t)=\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}(t))$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with components $\boldsymbol{f}=(f_1,f_2)^{\top}$, when is a vector $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ an equilibrium?
The solution of $x'(t)=-x(t)$ with $x(0)=3$ is $x(t)=3\mathrm{e}^{-t}$, and $x^*=0$ is the equilibrium of this equation. At which time $t\ge0$ does this solution equal $0$?
options: At no finite time, since $3\mathrm{e}^{-t}>0$ for every $t$
At $t=3$, the time given by the initial value
At $t=1$, after one unit of time at rate $-x$

questions.question: For the autonomous equation $x'(t)=f(x(t))$, the continuous function $f$ satisfies $f(x)\ge1$ for every real $x$, as for $f(x)=1+x^2$. Which statement about equilibria and solutions is correct?
options: The point where $f$ is smallest is an equilibrium
Solutions increase until they reach an equilibrium
Solutions decrease wherever the function $f$ is decreasing
There is no equilibrium, and every solution is strictly increasing

questions.question: The constant function $x(t)\equiv4$ solves the autonomous differential equation $x'(t)=f(x(t))$ for a given differentiable function $f$. What follows about $f$?
Consider $x'(t)=a\,x(t)+b$ in the degenerate case $a=0$, so that $x'(t)=b$ for a real constant $b$. What are the equilibria?
options: None if $b\neq0$, and every real number if $b=0$
Exactly one, $x^*=b$, the value of the rate
Exactly one, $x^*=-b/a$, as for any linear equation

questions.question: What is the equilibrium of the linear equation $x'(t)=6-3x(t)$?
Which set contains exactly the equilibria of the autonomous equation $x'(t)=x(t)^2-4x(t)+3$?
For the logistic equation $x'(t)=x(t)\big(1-x(t)\big)$ with equilibria $0$ and $1$, a solution starts at $x(0)=1.5$. How does this solution behave for $t\ge0$?
options: It stays at $1.5$, since it starts above both equilibria

questions.question: For $\boldsymbol{x}'(t)=A\boldsymbol{x}(t)+\boldsymbol{b}$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(-4,-1)^{\top}$, which vector is the equilibrium $\boldsymbol{x}^*$?
Every solution of $x'=ax+b$ with $a\neq0$ satisfies $x(t)-x^*=\mathrm{e}^{at}\big(x(0)-x^*\big)$, where $x^*$ is the equilibrium. What is the solution of $x'(t)=-3x(t)+6$ with $x(0)=5$?

For $x'(t)=f(x(t))$ with $f$ continuously differentiable, the only equilibria are $0$ and $1$, and $f>0$ on $(0,1)$. A solution starts at $x(0)=0.5$. Which statement about it is guaranteed for all $t\ge0$ in its domain?
options: It increases, reaches $1$ at some time and then stays at $1$
It increases and stays strictly between $0$ and $1$
It increases and may pass beyond $1$ if $f$ is large on $(0,1)$
It may oscillate inside $(0,1)$, since $f$ varies there

questions.question: For the autonomous equation $x'(t)=f(x(t))$ the function $f$ is continuous with $f(1)=-1$ and $f(2)=3$. What can be concluded about equilibria?
options: There is an equilibrium exactly at $x^*=1.25$
There is no equilibrium between $1$ and $2$, since $f$ changes sign
A solution starting at $x(0)=1$ will increase to $2$
There is at least one equilibrium strictly between $1$ and $2$

questions.question: For $x'(t)=a\,x(t)+b$ with $a\neq0$, let $x^*=-b/a$ be the equilibrium and define the deviation $y(t)=x(t)-x^*$. Which differential equation does $y$ satisfy?
For the non-autonomous equation $x'(t)=t\,x(t)-2t$, which constant functions $x(t)\equiv c$ are solutions on $\mathbb{R}$?
options: Every constant, since the right side vanishes at $t=0$
Only $x\equiv2$, which makes $t\,x-2t$ zero for every $t$
Only $x\equiv0$, since then the factor $x$ vanishes
None, because non-autonomous equations have no constant solutions

questions.question: The equation $x'(t)=\big(x(t)-1\big)^2$ has the single equilibrium $1$. How do the solutions starting at $x(0)=0$ and at $x(0)=2$ behave for $t\ge0$ while they exist?
options: The one from $0$ increases and the one from $2$ decreases
Both decrease, since $f$ is decreasing to the left of $1$
Both increase; the one from $0$ passes $1$ and goes on
Both increase; the one from $0$ stays below $1$

questions.question: The function $x(t)=5-2\mathrm{e}^{-3t}$ solves a linear equation $x'(t)=a\,x(t)+b$ with constants $a\neq0$ and $b$. Which equation is it?

For $x'(t)=-2\sqrt{|x(t)|}$ with $x(0)=1$, the function equal to $(1-t)^2$ for $0\le t\le1$ and to $0$ for $t\ge1$ is a solution, and $0$ is an equilibrium. Why can this solution reach the equilibrium in finite time?
options: Every solution reaches its equilibrium in finite time
$0$ is not really an equilibrium, as $f$ is not smooth there
The function stops being a solution once it is constant
$f(x)=-2\sqrt{|x|}$ is not differentiable at $0$, so no-touching fails

questions.question: For $x'(t)=f(x(t))$ with $f$ continuously differentiable, a solution satisfies $x(0)=1$ and $x(5)=3$. What can be concluded about equilibria in the interval $[1,3]$?
options: None in $(1,3)$, but $3$ itself may be one
There must be one, where the solution turns around
Nothing can be concluded without knowing $f$

questions.question: For $\boldsymbol{x}'(t)=A\boldsymbol{x}(t)+\boldsymbol{b}$ with $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1)^{\top}$, which statement about equilibria is correct?
options: There is none, since $A\boldsymbol{x}=-\boldsymbol{b}$ is inconsistent
There is a whole line of equilibria
The origin $\boldsymbol{0}$ is the only equilibrium

questions.question: A fish stock follows $x'(t)=x(t)\big(1-x(t)\big)-h$, where $h\ge0$ is a constant harvesting rate. For which values of $h$ does this equation have at least one equilibrium?
